prompt: Implement curry, uncurry and partial: convert a BiFunction into a chain of single-argument Functions and back again, so arguments can be supplied one at a time.
explanation: Currying rewrites a two-argument function as a one-argument function that returns another one-argument function, which is why the type is Function<A, Function<B, R>> and the lambda is the nested a -> b -> f.apply(a, b). The outer lambda captures f and the inner one captures a, so nothing is computed until the final apply supplies b. Partial application falls straight out of this: applying only the first argument leaves a reusable function that already remembers it.
hints: In Java a nested lambda a -> b -> something is legal and is read as a -> (b -> something).
uncurry goes the other way: take (a, b) and call f.apply(a) to get the inner function, then apply(b) on that.
partial does not need its own lambda at all -- curry(f).apply(a) already IS the waiting function.
